title: [PDF] Practice guideline update summary: Mild cognitive impairment | Semantic Scholar
abstract:
In patients with MCI, exercise training (6 months) is likely to improve cognitive measures and cognitive training may improve cognitive Measures, and no high-quality evidence exists to support pharmacologic treatments for MCI. Objective To update the 2001 American Academy of Neurology (AAN) guideline on mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

Objective To update the 2001 American Academy of Neurology (AAN) guideline on mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
Using data from the Italian Longitudinal Study on Aging (ILSA), Di Carlo et al. reported a higher prevalence of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) than the authors reported in this same elderly population (3.2%) and this diagnosis did not exclude subjects with mild impairment on activities of daily living and instrumental activities ofdaily living.Expand
Additional considerations are proposed when updating guidelines for the management of mild cognitive impairment, including predictable biomarkers, revising treatment option after additional clinical trials for cholinesterase inhibitors, and detailed regimes for lifestyle interventions.Expand
There is a need for national guidance on the use of neuroimaging, fluid biomarkers, cognitive testing, follow-up and diagnostic terminology in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), with growing evidence that these may also help guide prognosis.Expand
